sections.content: My eyepos function was broken (it was merging rows). But from the output of transitions 2–17, I can see that this is the history of LEVEL 1 (eyes moving up from row 49 to row 9). The reset event in level 2 should be a later transition. Let me find it: in level 2, the eyes were at (34,10)/(34,50), and after DOWN they were at (10,22)/(10,38). Let me search the transitions for large row jumps within level 2.

sections.label: TOOL CALL: python
sections.content:
<tool_call>
<function=python>
<parameter=code>
def eyepos(fr):
    lines = fr.ascii.split('\n')
    cells=[]
    for r in range(64):
        for i,ch in enumerate(lines[r]):
            if ch=='S': cells.append((r,i))
    if not cells: return []
    # cluster by column gap
    cells.sort()
    clusters=[]
    for r,c in cells:
        placed=False
        for cl in clusters:
            if any(abs(r-r2)<=4 and abs(c-c2)<=8 for r2,c2 in cl):
                cl.append((r,c)); placed=True; break
        if not placed: clusters.append([(r,c)])
    res=[]
    for cl in clusters:
        rs=[x[0] for x in cl]; cs=[x[1] for x in cl]
        res.append((min(rs),min(cs),max(cs)))
    return sorted(res)
for i,t in enumerate(transitions):
    e0 = eyepos(t.before_frame); e1 = eyepos(t.after_frame)
    if e0 and e1 and e0!=e1:
        dr = abs(e0[0][0]-e1[0][0])
        if dr>4:
            print(i, t.action, 'lvl', t.before_frame.level, e0, '->', e1)
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
